Meta’s Role in Gaming Today: Muse, VR, and UA
Skip to content
Weekly Digest
Meta’s Role in Gaming Today: Muse, VR, and UA
By Naavik •   October 18, 2026
Source:
Meta
A month after its personal productivity agent Muse
hit number one on the App Store
, Meta used its
Connect 2026 event
to state its priorities: AI first, glasses second, VR a distant third. But that list is missing arguably the most consequential story for game developers: Meta’s slow return as a preeminent gaming UA channel. Growing engagement with video products like Reels is a double-edged sword for gaming: Facebook and Instagram’s growth lets publishers reach more potential players, but those same products compete relentlessly with games for users’ attention.
Right now, Meta’s gaming-oriented metaverse investments are in a down cycle: the Quest hardware and
Horizon UGC platform
are clearly deprioritized, while its role in gaming UA is gaining momentum. And while glasses and Muse are clearly areas of investment today, the company has yet to connect them to gaming use cases.
Meta Is (Back as) a Games UA Engine
Since Apple introduced App Tracking Transparency (ATT), Meta has not been the dominant growth channel for mobile gaming. That is changing rapidly: in 2025, Meta grew its
share of gaming ad impressions on social media from 54% to 69%
, while TikTok’s share nearly halved (21.0→12.7%) and YouTube fell at a similar rate (20.0→12.0%). The company is outcompeting its social media rivals not only by growing impressions but also by improving price per ad (across all verticals, not just gaming), which rose
12% in 2026
. Meta’s ad business is growing in both volume and efficiency, an impressive feat that
suggests its underlying Recommendation System is becoming more efficient at driving engagement and allocating ads
.
ATT hit Meta particularly hard
; it relied on the deprecated IDFA for targeting gaming ads far more than competitors like AppLovin, and ultimately ceded much of the vertical to them,
winding down its once-grand dedicated gaming ads team
and prioritizing e-commerce until quite recently.
Meta’s gaming ad impressions in 2026 YTD already exceed those of any full year since 2020 | Source:
Pathmatics (Sensor Tower)
Since 2024, Meta has been building the capabilities needed to recapture a large share of gaming UA. These include
incrementality optimization (Q4 2024), LTVision (2024), AMM (reinstated in July 2025 after being shuttered in October 2021), and pLTV postback / “Value Optimization for Non-Purchase Events” (beta in 2025)
; Andromeda retrieval/ranking and Advantage+ as the default for App Promotion; and, importantly,
rebuilding the dedicated gaming ads organization, now based in London
, to work directly with publishers globally.
What does Meta’s return mean for gaming publishers? On the bright side, a new, high-performing channel is welcome. Unlike AppLovin, Unity, and other gaming-focused ad networks, Meta delivers impressions outside of games. Meanwhile,
the biggest drawback of gaming networks is that they may shuffle an existing pool of game players
. Many game studios also hide ads from their highest-LTV players, creating the risk of adverse selection.
Meta avoids this problem structurally. Everyone sees ads on social media, not just low-LTV players. Meta’s post-ATT ad products also help expose gaming ads to users most likely to spend in mobile games. Of course, Meta is not the only player in social media, but its share of social media engagement and
gaming ad impressions has increased significantly at the expense of rivals like TikTok and YouTube
, making Meta an increasingly important channel for reaching the most valuable players.
The VR Platform Dream Keeps Fizzling
Meta’s upcoming VR Glasses | Source:
IGN
Meta’s ads business is newly re-optimized for serving game publishers, but the same cannot be said for its Reality Labs business, which houses both its VR gaming and Horizon UGC efforts. Meta not only changed its name to signal its long-term bet on metaverse-like products but also sank
$88B into the division between 2020 and 2026
. Since then, it has hedged this bet considerably. Of the nine VR / gaming studios it acquired (such as
Sanzaru, Twisted Pixel, and Armature
), most have been closed or reduced to a skeleton crew. Sequels to VR “hits” like Arkham Shadow were canceled, and 2026 Connect had “
no big-budget exclusive of the kind Meta used to put in the Quest box
.”
Meta has been refocusing its hardware away from the gaming-oriented Quest line of headsets and towards glasses. Meta’s augmented-reality Ray-Ban glasses have sold well and received heavy promotion since
their September 2023 launch
. The most recent product, announced at this year’s Connect, is the aptly named “
VR Glasses
.”
Meta’s VR Glasses prioritize media and productivity | Source:
Meta
Although still a VR device, the VR Glasses are positioned as “
a different product for a different market
,” according to VP of VR Ryan Cairns. The VR Glasses are clearly a competitor to the Apple Vision Pro and are meant for casual VR entertainment that requires little local computing power. This helps explain why the announcement barely mentioned gaming, with only one sentence: “
more than 75 games at launch that you can play solely with hand gestures, and with Xbox Cloud Gaming, you can stream hundreds more
.”
The
developer page for the product
explicitly recommends casual and social mechanics over “virtual locomotion or gun-based gameplay.” This reflects the expectation that most users will rely on hand-tracking rather than dedicated controllers. In
Meta’s current catalog
, there are 123 titles that support hand-tracking input (including 19 ‘Coming Soon’ titles featuring well-known IP such as Tetris, Two Point Hospital, Ace Attorney, and Project Hail Mary).
